summary: Two disposable loopback servers were started: a TLS origin holding a short-lived self-signed certificate for one fixed hostname, and a plaintext target that appends every received request (method, path, headers) to a JSON-lines log. One GET with a Basic credential pair followed a 302 from the TLS origin to the plaintext target on the same hostname. The target log contains the hop with 'Authorization: Basic <base64 of the pair>' and the session finished with status 200. The credential crossed the plaintext wire exactly as the hostname-only predicate predicts; the falsifier (header absent) did not occur.
next_hint: The leak is confirmed at wire level on the vulnerable copy. The next step is to repair the redirect-auth rebuild step: keep the Authorization header only when the redirect target preserves scheme, hostname and effective port (substituting implicit default ports when omitted), replacing the hostname-only comparison while leaving the netrc re-lookup untouched; then prove the same fixture no longer forwards the header and that same-origin redirects still do. Fixture and certificate remain available; loopback ports only.
